titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 4/2007 (އޯޑިޓު ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ...... ވަނަ އިސްލާހު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This bill amends the Audit Act (Law No. 4/2007). It adds a new sub-article after an existing paragraph of Article 9. The new provision deals with performance reports from the bodies the Auditor General audits, including a time limit of 90 days and another of 30 days, and a fine of MVR 5,000 for breaking the rules. The explanatory note is followed by a list of 26 numbered entries (apparently institutions or groups of institutions), and those could not be read reliably. The scans are hard to read, so some details are uncertain.
whyItMatters: If passed, public bodies that fall under the Auditor General's audit would have deadlines to produce reports, with a fine if they miss them, which would make it easier for the public to see how they perform.
keyProvisions: Clause 1 adds a new sub-article to Article 9 of the Audit Act, numbered as a '-1' paragraph after an existing paragraph.
Sub-article (1) sets out a duty tied to the end of a 1 year period, with a time limit of 90 days.
Sub-article (2) sets a shorter time limit of 30 days.
Sub-article (3) says that failing to comply with (1) and (2) can be punished with a fine of MVR 5,000.
The explanatory note is followed by a numbered list of 26 entries, which could not be read well enough to describe.
Clause 2 is a short commencement clause, saying when the amendment takes effect once it is ratified and published.
whoIsAffected: State institutions and statutory bodies that the Auditor General audits, and the public that relies on those audits.
statedReasons: The explanatory note refers to the Auditor General's audit of state offices and statutory bodies, but the scan was too hard to read for the reasons to be stated reliably.
